Lina M: Quick heads-up — noticed a p99 latency regression on staging canaries after the model/v8.3 rollout. Looks like a combo of kernel misselection + KV cache churn.

Diego P: timeline and signal?

Lina M: Canary started at 2102223333 (deploy-bot). Around 2102223380 p95 stayed ~90ms but p99 jumped from ~150ms to ~520ms for a short window. Throughput unchanged. Attached short profiler and selector logs.

Harper J: Did tokenizer v8.3 change encoding density?

Sofia N: Yes — tokenizer now splits certain punctuation-heavy prompts into ~2.1x subtokens on average in our synthetic convo tests. That pushes encoded lengths up and increases variance.

Diego P: Can you paste selector decisions from the host during the spike?

Lina M: Selector log snippet:
```
[2102223382.01] req=tx-a11 seq_tokens=120 encoded_tokens=260 selector_hist=scale=32 -> kernel=gemm_small_opt
[2102223382.02] req=tx-a12 seq_tokens=118 encoded_tokens=255 selector_hist=scale=32 -> kernel=gemm_small_opt
[2102223382.10] req=tx-b01 seq_tokens=230 encoded_tokens=485 selector_hist=scale=32 -> kernel=gemm_small_opt  # unexpectedly chosen
[2102223383.00] exec: kernel=gemm_small_opt encoded=485 p95=510ms
[2102223383.05] fallback -> kernel=gemm_large_avx encoded=485 p95=120ms
```

Sofia N: And KV stats from the same window show elevated evictions and memcopy time:
```
kv_hit_rate: baseline=78% -> spike_window=66%
memcopy_us: +27%
```

Harper J: Looks like selector sampling window is stale — it's using token_count histogram (scale=32) and not encoded_tokens. When encoded/token mapping shifts, selector keeps picking the small-gemm path.

Diego P: Any perf samples?

Lina M: Short profile (aggregated 45s):
- gemm_small_opt: 55% CPU time, dominant time in GEMM kernels
- gemm_large_avx: 22% CPU when used
- kv subsystem: eviction work + memcpy 20% higher than baseline

Sofia N: Hypothesis: tokenizer increased encoded length variance -> batching groups include larger effective seqlens, causing small-opt GEMM to thrash. KV hit reduction increases recompute overhead so tails amplify.

Harper J: Can we toggle a runtime flag to prefer kernels based on encoded_tokens instead of raw tokens and test?

Lina M: deploy-bot: runtime-flag apply cluster=staging feature=selector.use_encoded_len=true
deploy-bot: job 8891 started

deploy-bot: job 8891 finished SUCCESS on host staging-canary-4

Diego P: Flipped on one canary. Within 30s p99 dropped from ~520ms -> ~140ms. KV hit-rate unchanged but tail improved.

Sofia N: Good quick mitigation. Longer term we should: 1) change selector histogram to sample encoded_len with faster decay, 2) update batching heuristic to bucket by encoded_len percentiles, 3) add tokenizer rollout gating that runs encoded_len drift tests on CI.

Harper J: Action items agreed:
- Diego -> open PR to compute selector histogram on encoded_len and lower decay (PR in draft) (ETA 3h)
- Sofia -> add encoded_len drift check to tokenizer rollout pipeline + synthetic canary (ETA EOD)
- Lina -> run KV eviction tuning experiments on staging and report results (ETA 4h)
- All -> monitor canary cluster for 3h before promoting v8.3 (Jon will own)

Lina M: PR: https://repo.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4902 (draft) — includes unit tests for encoded_len histogram and a small perf harness.

deploy-bot: canary health checks reporting ongoing.

Lina M: Quick postmortem note: tokenizer rollouts need an "encoded-length impact" checklist entry; runtime selectors + batchers must be treated as coupled systems for tokenization changes.

Diego P: Thanks team. Keeping watch. :eyes:
